Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, the answer is that surrogates of injury severity, including days in the ICU and non-ICU hospital LOS (>10 days), were associated with the development of heterotopic ossification (HO) in patients with acetabular fractures. Prophylaxis with X-ray (surveillance) was significantly protective against the development of HO, suggesting that severe injuries may be more likely to result in HO.

In summary, while not explicitly stated in all matches, the majority of evidence suggests that surrogates of injury severity are associated with a higher risk of heterotopic ossification in acetabular fractures. This is consistent with the conclusion drawn from a study that found that patients with longer ICU stays and greater LOS (>10 days) were more likely to develop HO. Therefore, healthcare providers should be aware of these factors when assessing for potential complications such as HO in patients with acetabular fractures.
